high.title: VNDirect Forecasts VN-Index Could Break 2,000 Points; Identifies Sectors with Momentum in H2 2026
high.summary:
VNDirect has released a macro and market strategy report projecting that the VN-Index could surpass the psychologically significant 2,000-point level in H2 2026, following a challenging first half marked by global macro headwinds. The brokerage identifies a convergence of supportive catalysts: Vietnam's official upgrade by FTSE Russell to emerging market status, ongoing market infrastructure reforms, a stable macroeconomic backdrop, and strong corporate earnings growth. VNDirect forecasts net profit growth for HoSE-listed companies could surge by up to 21% in full-year 2026, with momentum spread broadly across key sectors. The FTSE upgrade is particularly significant for international fund managers, as it is expected to trigger passive and active capital inflows from foreign institutional investors who were previously restricted or underweight on frontier-market Vietnam. This represents a structural positive for both Vietnamese equities and, indirectly, for VND stability, as sustained foreign equity inflows support the balance of payments. **Key watch points:** timing and scale of FTSE-linked inflows, foreign net buying trends on HoSE, and whether the VN-Index can sustain a breakout above 1,900 as a precursor to the 2,000 target.

---

high.title: Foreign Investors Return to Net Selling of VND 3,000 Billion in the First Week of Q3 — Which Stocks Were in Focus?
high.summary: Foreign investors resumed sustained net selling pressure on Vietnamese equities during the trading week of June 29 – July 3, offloading a cumulative net VND 3,007 billion (~USD 118–120 million) across all exchanges. The bulk of selling was concentrated on HoSE (VND 2,846 billion net sold), with marginal net buying on HNX (+VND 32 billion) and net selling on UPCoM (VND 193 billion). The VN-Index closed the week down 9.83 points (-0.53%) at 1,862.08 points, trading within a narrow 1,850–1,880 range with below-average liquidity.

medium.title: Why Are 2 Stocks Formerly Linked to Nguyen Ho Nam Facing Mandatory Delisting?
medium.summary:
The Ho Chi Minh Stock Exchange (HOSE) has issued mandatory delisting notices to Bamboo Capital Group (BCG) and Tracodi Construction Group (TCD). BCG faces delisting due to failure to publish multiple required financial reports, including audited annual reports for 2024 and 2025, as well as quarterly and semi-annual reports. TCD, while having submitted its audited financials for 2024 and 2025, faces delisting because its auditor (A&C Audit and Consulting Co.) issued a disclaimer of opinion on those reports — a trigger for mandatory delisting under current HOSE regulations. Both stocks will be transferred to the UPCoM market following their removal from HOSE. This is relevant for international investors as it signals continued enforcement of listing standards and corporate governance requirements by Vietnamese regulators, a positive long-term signal for market integrity ahead of the FTSE upgrade. Foreign funds with exposure to either stock should assess downside liquidity risk upon transfer to UPCoM.

---

medium.title: Why You Shouldn't Only Deposit Money at the Bank with the Highest Interest Rate
medium.summary: As of early July 2026, several Vietnamese banks continue to offer elevated deposit rates, though the headline figures come with highly restrictive conditions. PVcomBank leads the market at 10%/year for 12–13 month terms, but this rate is exclusively accessible to depositors with balances of VND 2,000 billion (≈USD 78M+) or more — effectively ruling out retail participation. MSB offers 9%/year for 12–13 month tenors, requiring a minimum balance of VND 500 billion. Nam A Bank offers 8.3%/year for 24-month deposits above VND 500 billion. The article cautions retail investors against chasing the highest headline rates without scrutinizing eligibility criteria. **Market relevance:** The persistence of high deposit rates at smaller banks signals continued competition for liquidity in Vietnam's banking system. For bond investors, elevated bank deposit yields — even if restricted to large-ticket depositors — exert upward pressure on the opportunity cost of holding government bonds, particularly at the short-to-medium end of the curve. Fund managers should monitor whether these rates begin to filter into broader retail deposit benchmarks.

medium.title: Prime Minister Appoints New Director General of Vietnam Bank for Social Policies
medium.summary: On June 29, 2026, Deputy Prime Minister Nguyen Van Thang signed Decision No. 1169/QĐ-TTg appointing Ms. Nguyen Thi Hang as Member of the Board of Directors and Director General of the Vietnam Bank for Social Policies (VBSP), effective July 1, 2026. Ms. Hang, born in 1978 and a native of Bac Ninh province, holds master's and bachelor's degrees in law, economics, and finance-banking, along with advanced political theory qualifications. She previously served as Director of VBSP's Ninh Binh branch and as Deputy Director General of VBSP. **Market relevance:** While VBSP is a policy-oriented institution rather than a commercial bank, leadership transitions at state-directed lenders can signal shifts in the government's credit policy priorities — particularly regarding subsidized lending programs that affect overall credit growth and monetary transmission. Low direct impact on VND or bond markets near-term, but worth monitoring for any policy mandate changes.

medium.title: Fuel Prices Cut Across the Board Effective This Afternoon, July 2nd
medium.summary:
Vietnam's Ministry of Industry & Trade and Ministry of Finance jointly implemented a scheduled fuel price adjustment on July 2nd, resulting in broad-based price cuts. E5 RON92 petrol fell VND 1,055/litre to a ceiling of VND 19,730/litre, while E10 RON95-III dropped VND 788/litre to VND 20,415/litre. Diesel eased VND 690/litre to VND 21,176/litre, and mazut (fuel oil) declined VND 977/kg. Notably, this marks the **second fuel price adjustment within a single week**, following a sharp increase on the evening of July 1st — when E5 RON92 had surged VND 1,426/litre. Authorities opted not to draw from the price stabilization fund but did allocate fresh contributions to it (VND 200/litre for petrol and diesel; VND 400/kg for mazut, sourced from the state budget). **Relevance:** The high intra-week fuel price volatility — a large increase followed almost immediately by a cut — reflects continued pass-through sensitivity from global crude oil swings. For macro watchers, fuel price dynamics feed directly into Vietnam's CPI calculation, which in turn influences the State Bank of Vietnam's (SBV) policy rate stance and its tolerance for VND depreciation. A deflationary impulse from lower pump prices could provide the SBV with modest room to maintain accommodative monetary conditions and ease pressure on the VND.

---

medium.title: Silver Recovers on New Fed Signals; Domestic Price Surpasses VND 62 Million/kg
medium.summary: Global silver prices rebounded in Thursday's session, crossing USD 59/ounce after hitting a seven-month low in prior sessions. The recovery was driven by Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's comments that inflation expectations have declined over the past month, signaling no immediate urgency to raise interest rates — a dovish tilt that broadly weakened the USD. Additionally, weaker-than-expected U.S. private sector job creation data reinforced expectations that the Fed will remain cautious on further rate adjustments. Domestically, silver prices in Vietnam crossed the VND 62 million/kg threshold.

medium.title: HoSE Removes 59 Securities from Margin Trading Eligibility in Q3 2026 — HVN, DGC, BCG and Multiple "Hot" Stocks Included
medium.summary:
Ho Chi Minh Stock Exchange (HoSE) has officially announced a list of 59 securities ineligible for margin trading in Q3 2026. The disqualified names span several categories: stocks under warning, control, restriction, or trading suspension (including HVN, DGC, BCG, LDG, OGC, TTF); newly listed securities with less than six months of trading history (e.g., AAN, ANT, GEL, KLB, and several ETFs including FUEMITEC and FUEVN50G); and companies reporting negative after-tax profit attributable to parent shareholders on audited 2025 financials (DAH, HAP, SPM, ST8, TNH, VPH). For equity investors, this is a meaningful liquidity signal — margin restrictions reduce speculative buying capacity in affected names and can trigger forced selling pressure. International fund managers monitoring the VN-Index should note that concentrated margin cuts in "hot" stocks may dampen near-term momentum in those counters and add volatility to the broader market. Watch for any secondary spillover into banking stocks that provide margin financing.

medium.title: New SBV Circular 29/2026: Sweeping New Bank Lending Rules to Take Effect August 15, 2026
medium.summary: The State Bank of Vietnam (SBV) has issued Circular 29/2026/TT-NHNN, amending Circular 39/2016/TT-NHNN on credit institution lending activities, effective **August 15, 2026**. Key changes include: (1) **Small-value loan thresholds** are redefined — up to VND 200 million at people's credit funds and up to **VND 400 million** at other credit institutions — with simplified documentation requirements (borrowers no longer need to submit a viable capital-use plan, only basic proof of lawful fund usage and financial capacity); (2) A new **debt repayment priority rule** mandates that **principal must be collected before interest** on all overdue loans, a significant shift in how banks handle delinquent accounts. For bond and equity investors, this regulatory tightening signals the SBV's continued effort to manage credit quality and reduce systemic risk within the banking sector. The simplified small-loan rules could modestly **stimulate retail credit growth**, while the principal-first repayment rule may pressure near-term **bank profitability metrics and NPL recognition**. Watch for bank earnings guidance revisions heading into Q3 2026.

medium.title: Gold Bar and Ring Prices Surge Over VND 3 Million/Tael on Afternoon of July 3
medium.summary: Domestic gold prices surged sharply on the afternoon of July 3, with major retailers (SJC, PNJ, DOJI, Bảo Tín Mạnh Hải) simultaneously raising prices by VND 3–3.3 million/tael. Gold bars are now quoted at **VND 148.4–151.4 million/tael** (buy/sell), while gold rings reached **VND 151.5 million/tael** at some retailers. The move tracks a global gold rally. For FX and macro watchers, a sustained surge in domestic gold prices is relevant as a **proxy for USD demand** — Vietnamese consumers and investors historically purchase gold using USD or convert VND to USD to access international gold markets, which can create **mild upward pressure on USD/VND**. The SBV has in the past intervened in the gold market to prevent excessive gold-USD arbitrage. If gold prices remain elevated, monitor whether the SBV signals any administrative intervention or quota adjustments on gold imports.
